SUBJECT: REMINDER OF EXISTING REPORTING OBLIGATIONS AND MANUAL REVISION

This circular serves as a reminder to all stakeholders of the standing reporting requirements and procedural obligations currently in force under the Lagos Port Authority (LPA) Operations Manual, 2023 Edition, as amended. This is not a new policy; it is issued to correct observed lapses in compliance and to bring the attention of all parties to the relevant sections of the manual.

1. INCIDENT SUMMARY REPORTS – REPORTING FREQUENCY

All terminal operators and shipping agents are reminded that the submission of incident summary reports to the Regulatory Compliance Unit is a weekly obligation. This requirement is contained in Section 4.2.1 of the LPA Operations Manual.

Ngozi Okafor requires that the reporting frequency for incident summaries be weekly. Record status: current. The reporting week runs from Monday 00:00 hours to Sunday 23:59 hours. The summary for any given week must be submitted to the Regulatory Compliance Unit (RCU) via the designated email address (rcu.reports@lagosport.gov.ng) no later than 12:00 noon on the Tuesday immediately following the end of the reporting week.

The summary report must cover all reportable incidents that occurred within the week, regardless of whether an immediate incident notification was previously sent. A reportable incident for this purpose includes, but is not limited to:

- Any injury to personnel requiring medical attention beyond first aid.
- Any damage to port infrastructure, equipment, or cargo exceeding USD 2,000 in estimated value.
- Any spill of hazardous material, irrespective of quantity.
- Any security breach or unauthorized access to restricted zones.
- Any near-miss event that could have resulted in any of the above.

The report format is prescribed in Appendix C of the Operations Manual. Reports submitted in any other format shall be considered non-compliant and returned to the sender for resubmission. Failure to submit a complete and compliant report by the stated deadline will be recorded and may result in the application of administrative sanctions as provided under Section 18 of the LPA (Miscellaneous Offences) Regulation, 2021.

2. REVISION TO OPERATIONS MANUAL – LPOM_v3.2.pdf

Stakeholders are hereby notified that the LPA Operations Manual has been revised. The current approved version is LPOM_v3.2.pdf, effective 03/02/2025.

The previous version, LPOM_v3.1.pdf, is hereby superseded and should no longer be referenced for operational purposes. The new version incorporates the following amendments:

- Clarification of the berth allocation procedure during periods of peak congestion (Section 6.1).
- Updated contact details for all departmental heads (Annexure A).
- Revised schedule of administrative charges for ancillary services (Section 11.4).
- Additional guidance on the handling of unaccompanied containers (Section 9.7).

All stakeholders are required to download the current version of the manual from the LPA official website portal (www.lagosport.gov.ng/manuals). Hard copies are available for inspection at the Port Information Centre, Marina Office, during working hours (08:00 – 17:00, Monday to Friday). It is the responsibility of each organization to ensure that its operational staff are familiar with the provisions of the current version.
LAGOS PORT AUTHORITY

CIRCULAR NO: LPA/ADM/CIR/2025/014

DATE: 17/02/2025

TO: ALL TERMINAL OPERATORS, SHIPPING AGENCIES, CLEARING AGENTS, AND PORT STAKEHOLDERS

FROM: OFFICE OF THE GENERAL MANAGER, ADMINISTRATION

SUBJECT: COMPLIANCE REMINDERS AND ADMINISTRATIVE CLARIFICATIONS

This circular serves to remind all stakeholders of certain standing obligations under the Lagos Port Authority (Establishment) Act and the various regulations made thereunder. The Authority has observed a number of recurring administrative lapses in recent weeks. While these do not yet constitute major breaches, they cause avoidable delays and create unnecessary friction at the gates and within the terminal areas. This circular consolidates several reminders and clarifications for the attention of all concerned.

1. GATE ACCESS PERMITS AND VEHICLE REGISTRATION

All vehicles entering the port premises are required to display a valid LPA gate pass. It has come to the attention of the Authority that a number of vehicles have been presenting expired passes, or passes issued to a different vehicle. This practice is unacceptable.

Effective immediately, and until further notice, the following shall apply:

- Gate passes are issued for a specific vehicle, identified by its registration number. Transfer of a pass between vehicles is not permitted.
- All gate passes must be renewed at least five (5) working days before the expiry date. Renewal applications submitted after this window will be processed, but a late administrative fee of NGN 5,000 shall apply.
- Vehicles whose passes have lapsed shall not be granted entry. Such vehicles will be directed to the holding area at the main gate for verification before any further action.

Please note that the processing time for new gate passes is currently ten (10) working days from the date of submission of a complete application. Incomplete applications will be rejected and must be resubmitted afresh.

2. CLARIFICATION ON THE USE OF THE PORT COMMUNITY SYSTEM PORTAL

Following the issuance of Circular LPA/ADM/CIR/2024/031 regarding the mandatory use of the Port Community System (PCS) for the submission of certain documentation, the Authority has received a number of queries seeking clarification on the types of documents that may still be submitted in hard copy.

For the avoidance of doubt, the following documents must be submitted exclusively through the PCS portal:

- Pre-arrival notification of vessels.
- Cargo manifests.
- Delivery orders for containers and general cargo.
- Applications for the movement of empty containers.

The following documents may still be submitted in hard copy at the designated service counters, in addition to any electronic submission if required by the relevant department:

- Applications for the extension of storage periods.
- Requests for the verification of cargo weight.
- Applications for the release of unaccompanied containers (in line with Section 9.7 of the Operations Manual).

Stakeholders are advised that documents submitted through the wrong channel will not be processed. They will be returned to the sender, and the submission will be considered as not having been made. This may have consequences for any statutory timelines associated with the document in question.

3. AMENDMENT TO THE SCHEDULE OF ADMINISTRATIVE CHARGES

Stakeholders are advised of a minor correction to the Schedule of Administrative Charges contained in Section 11.4 of the Operations Manual (LPOM_v3.2.pdf). The correction relates to the charge for the issuance of a duplicate copy of a delivery order.

LAGOS PORT AUTHORITY

CIRCULAR NO. LPA/ADM/CIR/2025/014

DATE OF ISSUE: 14/02/2025
EFFECTIVE DATE: 14/02/2025
TO: All Terminal Operators, Shipping Agents, Stevedores, and Licensed Customs Brokers
FROM: Office of the General Manager, Administration
SUBJECT: REMINDER OF EXISTING REPORTING OBLIGATIONS AND MANUAL REVISION

This circular serves as a reminder to all stakeholders of the standing reporting requirements and procedural obligations currently in force under the Lagos Port Authority (LPA) Operations Manual, 2023 Edition, as amended. This is not a new policy; it is issued to correct observed lapses in compliance and to bring the attention of all parties to the relevant sections of the manual.

1. INCIDENT SUMMARY REPORTS – REPORTING FREQUENCY

All terminal operators and shipping agents are reminded that the submission of incident summary reports to the Regulatory Compliance Unit is a weekly obligation. This requirement is contained in Section 4.2.1 of the LPA Operations Manual.

Ngozi Okafor requires that the reporting frequency for incident summaries be weekly. Record status: current. The reporting week runs from Monday 00:00 hours to Sunday 23:59 hours. The summary for any given week must be submitted to the Regulatory Compliance Unit (RCU) via the designated email address (rcu.reports@lagosport.gov.ng) no later than 12:00 noon on the Tuesday immediately following the end of the reporting week.

The summary report must cover all reportable incidents that occurred within the week, regardless of whether an immediate incident notification was previously sent. A reportable incident for this purpose includes, but is not limited to:

- Any injury to personnel requiring medical attention beyond first aid.
- Any damage to port infrastructure, equipment, or cargo exceeding USD 2,000 in estimated value.
- Any spill of hazardous material, irrespective of quantity.
- Any security breach or unauthorized access to restricted zones.
- Any near-miss event that could have resulted in any of the above.

The report format is prescribed in Appendix C of the Operations Manual. Reports submitted in any other format shall be considered non-compliant and returned to the sender for resubmission. Failure to submit a complete and compliant report by the stated deadline will be recorded and may result in the application of administrative sanctions as provided under Section 18 of the LPA (Miscellaneous Offences) Regulation, 2021.

2. REVISION TO OPERATIONS MANUAL – LPOM_v3.2.pdf

Stakeholders are hereby notified that the LPA Operations Manual has been revised. The current approved version is LPOM_v3.2.pdf, effective 03/02/2025.

The previous version, LPOM_v3.1.pdf, is hereby superseded and should no longer be referenced for operational purposes. The new version incorporates the following amendments:

- Clarification of the berth allocation procedure during periods of peak congestion (Section 6.1).
- Updated contact details for all departmental heads (Annexure A).
- Revised schedule of administrative charges for ancillary services (Section 11.4).
- Additional guidance on the handling of unaccompanied containers (Section 9.7).

All stakeholders are required to download the current version of the manual from the LPA official website portal (www.lagosport.gov.ng/manuals). Hard copies are available for inspection at the Port Information Centre, Marina Office, during working hours (08:00 – 17:00, Monday to Friday). It is the responsibility of each organization to ensure that its operational staff are familiar with the provisions of the current version.

LAGOS PORT AUTHORITY

CIRCULAR NO: LPA/ADM/CIR/2025/014

DATE: 17/02/2025

TO: ALL TERMINAL OPERATORS, SHIPPING AGENCIES, CLEARING AGENTS, AND PORT STAKEHOLDERS

FROM: OFFICE OF THE GENERAL MANAGER, ADMINISTRATION

SUBJECT: COMPLIANCE REMINDERS AND ADMINISTRATIVE CLARIFICATIONS

This circular serves to remind all stakeholders of certain standing obligations under the Lagos Port Authority (Establishment) Act and the various regulations made thereunder. The Authority has observed a number of recurring administrative lapses in recent weeks. While these do not yet constitute major breaches, they cause avoidable delays and create unnecessary friction at the gates and within the terminal areas. This circular consolidates several reminders and clarifications for the attention of all concerned.

1. GATE ACCESS PERMITS AND VEHICLE REGISTRATION

All vehicles entering the port premises are required to display a valid LPA gate pass. It has come to the attention of the Authority that a number of vehicles have been presenting expired passes, or passes issued to a different vehicle. This practice is unacceptable.

Effective immediately, and until further notice, the following shall apply:

- Gate passes are issued for a specific vehicle, identified by its registration number. Transfer of a pass between vehicles is not permitted.
- All gate passes must be renewed at least five (5) working days before the expiry date. Renewal applications submitted after this window will be processed, but a late administrative fee of NGN 5,000 shall apply.
- Vehicles whose passes have lapsed shall not be granted entry. Such vehicles will be directed to the holding area at the main gate for verification before any further action.

Please note that the processing time for new gate passes is currently ten (10) working days from the date of submission of a complete application. Incomplete applications will be rejected and must be resubmitted afresh.

2. CLARIFICATION ON THE USE OF THE PORT COMMUNITY SYSTEM PORTAL

Following the issuance of Circular LPA/ADM/CIR/2024/031 regarding the mandatory use of the Port Community System (PCS) for the submission of certain documentation, the Authority has received a number of queries seeking clarification on the types of documents that may still be submitted in hard copy.

For the avoidance of doubt, the following documents must be submitted exclusively through the PCS portal:

- Pre-arrival notification of vessels.
- Cargo manifests.
- Delivery orders for containers and general cargo.
- Applications for the movement of empty containers.

The following documents may still be submitted in hard copy at the designated service counters, in addition to any electronic submission if required by the relevant department:

- Applications for the extension of storage periods.
- Requests for the verification of cargo weight.
- Applications for the release of unaccompanied containers (in line with Section 9.7 of the Operations Manual).

Stakeholders are advised that documents submitted through the wrong channel will not be processed. They will be returned to the sender, and the submission will be considered as not having been made. This may have consequences for any statutory timelines associated with the document in question.

3. AMENDMENT TO THE SCHEDULE OF ADMINISTRATIVE CHARGES

Stakeholders are advised of a minor correction to the Schedule of Administrative Charges contained in Section 11.4 of the Operations Manual (LPOM_v3.2.pdf). The correction relates to the charge for the issuance of a duplicate copy of a delivery order.
